startHere.title: What a quantum computer is doing in this book
startHere.hook: A classical program updates bits. In the circuit model used here, a quantum program applies reversible linear transformations to complex amplitude vectors and reads classical outcomes through measurement.
steps: Describe the information by complex amplitudes.
Apply a unitary matrix; this is the reversible evolution step.
Compose gates from left to right in time.
Convert amplitudes into classical outcome probabilities.
Use those ingredients to prepare useful states and embed useful non-unitary matrices into unitaries.

circuit.caption: A first two-qubit circuit: H creates a superposition and CNOT turns it into an entangled Bell pair.

linear-algebra.eyebrow: Beginner layer · before the formal matrix API
linear-algebra.title: A qubit is a two-entry complex vector
linear-algebra.hook: Do not start by thinking about a mysterious physical particle. For the algorithms in this library, start with two labels, |0⟩ and |1⟩, and attach a complex amplitude to each.
intuitionSteps: |0⟩ and |1⟩ are the two computational labels.
α and β are not probabilities; their squared magnitudes are.
The two measurement probabilities must add to one.
A quantum gate acts on the amplitude vector by matrix multiplication.

circuit.caption: A state before any gate: the wire carries a qubit state, not a classical hidden bit.

leanLens.title: Lean idea: finite indices
leanLens.code: abbrev Matrix (rows cols : Nat) (α : Type u) := Fin rows → Fin cols → α
leanLens.explanation: `Fin 2` means exactly two legal indices. Lean makes an out-of-range basis label impossible to type.

circuit-semantics.title: A quantum circuit is a time-ordered product of unitary gates
circuit-semantics.hook: A wire tells you where the state lives; a box tells you which operation happens next. Read time from left to right, but remember that matrix products act on state vectors from the right.
intuitionSteps: Place one operation after another on the wire.
Lean fixes this order once so diagrams and matrix proofs cannot silently disagree.

circuit.caption: A one-qubit circuit like the standard textbook examples.

leanLens.title: Lean idea: definitions compute
leanLens.code: evalGateMatrices [G₁, G₂, …, Gₘ] = Gₘ ⬝ … ⬝ G₂ ⬝ G₁
leanLens.explanation: The evaluator is a definition, and later theorems prove that circuit syntax and matrix meaning use the same order.

state-preparation.title: State preparation asks: which circuit creates the vector I want?
state-preparation.hook: You know the desired amplitudes. The construction problem is to find a unitary whose action on the easy input |0…0⟩ produces exactly those amplitudes.
intuitionSteps: Write the normalized amplitude vector you want.
Choose gates whose product might have that target as column zero.
Prove the whole matrix is unitary, not only that one column looks right.
Prove the zero-input column equals the target exactly.

circuit.caption: The smallest nontrivial preparation: Hadamard creates |+⟩.

leanLens.title: Lean idea: a certificate is a structure
leanLens.code:
structure ComplexStatePreparationCertificate where
  target
  gate
  normalizationProof
  preparationProof
leanLens.explanation: The circuit, target, and proofs travel together. A downstream theorem cannot accidentally forget normalization or unitarity.

state-preparation-certificates.eyebrow: Beginner layer · why the first column matters
state-preparation-certificates.title: Applying U to |0…0⟩ simply selects the first column of U
state-preparation-certificates.hook: This is the bridge between circuit language and matrix language. Physicists write U|0⟩; Lean can check the same statement one output amplitude at a time.
intuitionSteps: The vector |0…0⟩ has a single 1 in the zero position.
Every matrix column except column zero is multiplied by 0.
The output is exactly column zero.
That theorem becomes a compact interface for later LCU and oracle constructions.

circuit.caption: State-action and first-column views are the same certificate.

leanLens.title: Lean idea: `iff` proves two descriptions are equivalent
leanLens.explanation: The theorem is deliberately bidirectional: a column proof can become a state-action proof and vice versa.

block-encoding.title: A general matrix is not a quantum gate — block encoding hides it inside one
block-encoding.hook: Quantum gates must be unitary, but the matrix A you want to use may be non-unitary. The trick is to build a larger unitary U whose clean ancilla corner equals A up to a known scale.
intuitionSteps: A may shrink, amplify, or otherwise fail the unitary condition.
Introduce ancilla qubits so a larger matrix can remain unitary.
Arrange for the ancilla-zero block to be A/α.
Later algorithms can manipulate the encoded matrix while only implementing the unitary U_A.

circuit.caption: The ancilla is prepared and projected in |0⟩; the system sees the clean block A/α.

leanLens.title: Lean idea: projection equality is the acceptance test
leanLens.code: candidate.blockContainsTarget : ∀ i j, U (clean i) (clean j) = A i j / α
leanLens.explanation: The library does not accept a circuit because a simulator looks close. The selected matrix entries are an explicit proposition.

classic-routes.eyebrow: Beginner layer · how block encodings are constructed
classic-routes.title: PREPARE, SELECT, and UNPREPARE turn structured sums into circuits
classic-routes.hook: Most useful matrices have structure. Instead of synthesizing one enormous unitary from scratch, expose that structure: sparse locations, sparse values, permutations, or a linear combination of simpler unitaries.
intuitionSteps: Create a superposition over terms or sparse slots.
Apply the operation indexed by that slot.
Load the coefficient associated with the chosen term.
Interfere the selector branches so the clean block becomes the desired weighted sum.

circuit.caption: The standard LCU skeleton used repeatedly by block-encoding constructions.

leanLens.title: Lean idea: composition becomes reusable lemmas
leanLens.explanation: Instead of proving each paper from zero, ASPBE keeps small proof-producing constructors for recurring routes.

certified-cases.title: A proof is easier to understand when you can watch one basis state travel through the circuit
certified-cases.hook: The case studies are not decoration. Each one freezes a matrix, a register layout, and a circuit, then lets you compare the paper picture, the executable circuit, and the Lean theorem.
intuitionSteps: Name the exact finite target and normalization.
Follow clean basis inputs through the candidate circuit.
Promote only after unitarity and every clean-block entry are exact.
Only candidates at the same semantic tier may be compared by resources.

circuit.caption: Case-study reading order: target → circuit → clean block → resource comparison.

leanLens.title: Lean idea: theorem names are checkpoints
leanLens.explanation: A reader can jump from a diagram directly to the declaration that certifies the same stage.

resources-and-exports.eyebrow: Beginner layer · proof versus engineering evidence
resources-and-exports.title: A correct circuit and a cheap circuit are different questions
resources-and-exports.hook: First prove the mathematical contract. Then count gates, depth, ancillas, and oracle calls. Finally export exactly the certified gate list to Qiskit or OpenQASM for independent executable checks.
intuitionSteps: Lean proves the operator or state contract.
The resource tuple is computed from the declared circuit.
Qiskit/OpenQASM receive the same canonical circuit.
Numerical operator comparison can catch implementation bugs but does not replace the theorem.

circuit.caption: One source of truth feeds both formal and executable evidence.

leanLens.title: Lean idea: costs are data, dominance is a theorem
leanLens.explanation: When the site says one candidate is better, a named Lean theorem fixes the ordering and the compared tuples.

automation-and-roadmap.eyebrow: Beginner layer · what the agent system actually does
automation-and-roadmap.title: The harness proposes; Lean decides what becomes library memory
automation-and-roadmap.hook: An LLM can generate a plausible construction quickly. ASPBE separates that creative step from verification: failed routes are remembered, accepted routes carry exact proof roots, and only then are they exposed as reusable memory.
intuitionSteps: Upper agents propose decompositions or candidate circuits.
Executable backends reject obvious circuit mistakes early.
Lean discharges the exact semantic obligations.
Only proof-backed constructions enter positive reusable memory.

circuit.caption: The harness is a verification loop around circuit construction, not a replacement for the proof kernel.

leanLens.title: Lean idea: acceptance is a typed state transition
leanLens.explanation: The controller trace can reach `accepted` only through the reviewer stage with a recorded passing Lean gate.
